slides.title: Drug levels answer specific exposure and toxicity questions
slides.section: Drug levels answer specific exposure and toxicity questions
paragraphs: Routine TDM is most established for IV aminoglycosides. For oral drugs, consider it when poor response, malabsorption, major interactions or toxicity raises a specific question. A target concentration is not a guarantee of cure.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Drug levels answer specific exposure and toxicity questions Routine TDM is most established for IV aminoglycosides. For oral drugs, consider it when poor response, malabsorption, major interactions or toxicity raises a specific question. A target concentration is not a guarantee of cure. Use drug levels with a defined clinical question Situation Practical interpretation IV amikacin Use a pharmacy-designed dose, interval and sampling plan. Guideline reference doses are 10-15 mg/kg daily or 15-25 mg/kg three times weekly, adjusted by levels and renal function. Older/frail patients may require lower exposure. Amikacin concentrations Reference peak targets differ by schedule: about 35-45 mcg/mL with daily dosing and 65-80 mcg/mL with intermittent dosing. The guideline gives a trough below 5 mcg/mL; many NTM centers target an undetectable trough. Specify which approach is being used. Timing of amikacin levels Two postinfusion samples, often at approximately 2 and 6 hours after the infusion ends under a defined local protocol, can be used to back-extrapolate Cmax. Record infusion start/end and exact sample times. A late measured concentration is not directly interchangeable with an extrapolated peak. Long-term linezolid Consider TDM during prolonged treatment, especially with cytopenias, renal dysfunction, low body weight or other toxicity risk. Collect a true trough immediately before a dose at steady state, with exact dose and sample times. Published NTM pharmacotherapy guidance describes a trough below 2 mcg/mL (2 mg/L) as one approach for prolonged use. The 2025 TB guideline also uses this safety goal, but it is not a validated NTM efficacy target. Published TB exposure-toxicity data support concern above this range, but do not establish a universal NTM threshold. Repeat after dose changes or changing renal function. Interpret with MIC and companion-drug activity before reducing to 300 mg daily or another individualized schedule. Continue CBC, vision and neuropathy surveillance even when levels are low. Lowering an elevated level does not establish that toxicity risk has resolved. Selected oral-agent TDM Consider for unexpected failure or absorption/interactions. A low early level may reflect delayed absorption; paired later sampling can help. Coordinate assay availability and interpretation before ordering. Ethambutol and aminoglycosides need particular attention in renal dysfunction; adjust intervals rather than improvising low daily doses. Rifampin affects anticoagulants, ART and transplant medications. Rifabutin has fewer induction effects but is not interaction-free. QT-active combinations require an individualized ECG and electrolyte plan. Sources [1] [3] Where to send drug levels When the assay is unavailable in-house, arrange a send-out through the local laboratory before collection. The following are verified reference-laboratory options, not confirmation of an institution’s contracted destination or local order code. Public reference-laboratory options for linezolid TDM Laboratory Test and ordering resource Collection planning National Jewish Health, Advanced Diagnostic Laboratories Linezolid level: PKLZD; current test instructions . Telephone 800-550-6227. Plain red-top serum; preferred 2 mL serum, minimum 0.25 mL. Separate promptly, freeze and ship on dry ice according to current instructions. Listed analytical turnaround 2-3 days excludes transit. University of Florida, Infectious Disease Pharmacokinetics Laboratory (IDPL) Linezolid: LNZL. Current catalog and requisition ; telephone 352-273-6710. Confirm assay-specific volume and current collection/shipping requirements . The catalog includes other antimycobacterial drug assays. Specify whether the question is a trough or postdose exposure profile. Include exact dose, dosing interval, last administration time, infusion times if applicable, sample time, renal function and relevant MIC. Avoid gel-separator tubes unless explicitly accepted by the performing laboratory. Do not send an untimed “random” linezolid level and interpret it as a trough. Send-out turnaround does not replace prompt action for suspected serious toxicity. Sources [24] [20] [21] [22]

rows: Two postinfusion samples, often at approximately 2 and 6 hours after the infusion ends under a defined local protocol, can be used to back-extrapolate Cmax. Record infusion start/end and exact sample times. A late measured concentration is not directly interchangeable with an extrapolated peak.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Drug levels answer specific exposure and toxicity questions Routine TDM is most established for IV aminoglycosides. For oral drugs, consider it when poor response, malabsorption, major interactions or toxicity raises a specific question. A target concentration is not a guarantee of cure. Use drug levels with a defined clinical question Situation Practical interpretation IV amikacin Use a pharmacy-designed dose, interval and sampling plan. Guideline reference doses are 10-15 mg/kg daily or 15-25 mg/kg three times weekly, adjusted by levels and renal function. Older/frail patients may require lower exposure. Amikacin concentrations Reference peak targets differ by schedule: about 35-45 mcg/mL with daily dosing and 65-80 mcg/mL with intermittent dosing. The guideline gives a trough below 5 mcg/mL; many NTM centers target an undetectable trough. Specify which approach is being used. Timing of amikacin levels Two postinfusion samples, often at approximately 2 and 6 hours after the infusion ends under a defined local protocol, can be used to back-extrapolate Cmax. Record infusion start/end and exact sample times. A late measured concentration is not directly interchangeable with an extrapolated peak. Long-term linezolid Consider TDM during prolonged treatment, especially with cytopenias, renal dysfunction, low body weight or other toxicity risk. Collect a true trough immediately before a dose at steady state, with exact dose and sample times. Published NTM pharmacotherapy guidance describes a trough below 2 mcg/mL (2 mg/L) as one approach for prolonged use. The 2025 TB guideline also uses this safety goal, but it is not a validated NTM efficacy target. Published TB exposure-toxicity data support concern above this range, but do not establish a universal NTM threshold. Repeat after dose changes or changing renal function. Interpret with MIC and companion-drug activity before reducing to 300 mg daily or another individualized schedule. Continue CBC, vision and neuropathy surveillance even when levels are low. Lowering an elevated level does not establish that toxicity risk has resolved. Selected oral-agent TDM Consider for unexpected failure or absorption/interactions. A low early level may reflect delayed absorption; paired later sampling can help. Coordinate assay availability and interpretation before ordering. Ethambutol and aminoglycosides need particular attention in renal dysfunction; adjust intervals rather than improvising low daily doses. Rifampin affects anticoagulants, ART and transplant medications. Rifabutin has fewer induction effects but is not interaction-free. QT-active combinations require an individualized ECG and electrolyte plan. Sources [1] [3] Where to send drug levels When the assay is unavailable in-house, arrange a send-out through the local laboratory before collection. The following are verified reference-laboratory options, not confirmation of an institution’s contracted destination or local order code. Public reference-laboratory options for linezolid TDM Laboratory Test and ordering resource Collection planning National Jewish Health, Advanced Diagnostic Laboratories Linezolid level: PKLZD; current test instructions . Telephone 800-550-6227. Plain red-top serum; preferred 2 mL serum, minimum 0.25 mL. Separate promptly, freeze and ship on dry ice according to current instructions. Listed analytical turnaround 2-3 days excludes transit. University of Florida, Infectious Disease Pharmacokinetics Laboratory (IDPL) Linezolid: LNZL. Current catalog and requisition ; telephone 352-273-6710. Confirm assay-specific volume and current collection/shipping requirements . The catalog includes other antimycobacterial drug assays. Specify whether the question is a trough or postdose exposure profile. Include exact dose, dosing interval, last administration time, infusion times if applicable, sample time, renal function and relevant MIC. Avoid gel-separator tubes unless explicitly accepted by the performing laboratory. Do not send an untimed “random” linezolid level and interpret it as a trough. Send-out turnaround does not replace prompt action for suspected serious toxicity. Sources [24] [20] [21] [22]

paragraphs: Ethambutol and aminoglycosides need particular attention in renal dysfunction; adjust intervals rather than improvising low daily doses. Rifampin affects anticoagulants, ART and transplant medications. Rifabutin has fewer induction effects but is not interaction-free. QT-active combinations require an individualized ECG and electrolyte plan.
Sources [1] [3]
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Drug levels answer specific exposure and toxicity questions Routine TDM is most established for IV aminoglycosides. For oral drugs, consider it when poor response, malabsorption, major interactions or toxicity raises a specific question. A target concentration is not a guarantee of cure. Use drug levels with a defined clinical question Situation Practical interpretation IV amikacin Use a pharmacy-designed dose, interval and sampling plan. Guideline reference doses are 10-15 mg/kg daily or 15-25 mg/kg three times weekly, adjusted by levels and renal function. Older/frail patients may require lower exposure. Amikacin concentrations Reference peak targets differ by schedule: about 35-45 mcg/mL with daily dosing and 65-80 mcg/mL with intermittent dosing. The guideline gives a trough below 5 mcg/mL; many NTM centers target an undetectable trough. Specify which approach is being used. Timing of amikacin levels Two postinfusion samples, often at approximately 2 and 6 hours after the infusion ends under a defined local protocol, can be used to back-extrapolate Cmax. Record infusion start/end and exact sample times. A late measured concentration is not directly interchangeable with an extrapolated peak. Long-term linezolid Consider TDM during prolonged treatment, especially with cytopenias, renal dysfunction, low body weight or other toxicity risk. Collect a true trough immediately before a dose at steady state, with exact dose and sample times. Published NTM pharmacotherapy guidance describes a trough below 2 mcg/mL (2 mg/L) as one approach for prolonged use. The 2025 TB guideline also uses this safety goal, but it is not a validated NTM efficacy target. Published TB exposure-toxicity data support concern above this range, but do not establish a universal NTM threshold. Repeat after dose changes or changing renal function. Interpret with MIC and companion-drug activity before reducing to 300 mg daily or another individualized schedule. Continue CBC, vision and neuropathy surveillance even when levels are low. Lowering an elevated level does not establish that toxicity risk has resolved. Selected oral-agent TDM Consider for unexpected failure or absorption/interactions. A low early level may reflect delayed absorption; paired later sampling can help. Coordinate assay availability and interpretation before ordering. Ethambutol and aminoglycosides need particular attention in renal dysfunction; adjust intervals rather than improvising low daily doses. Rifampin affects anticoagulants, ART and transplant medications. Rifabutin has fewer induction effects but is not interaction-free. QT-active combinations require an individualized ECG and electrolyte plan. Sources [1] [3] Where to send drug levels When the assay is unavailable in-house, arrange a send-out through the local laboratory before collection. The following are verified reference-laboratory options, not confirmation of an institution’s contracted destination or local order code. Public reference-laboratory options for linezolid TDM Laboratory Test and ordering resource Collection planning National Jewish Health, Advanced Diagnostic Laboratories Linezolid level: PKLZD; current test instructions . Telephone 800-550-6227. Plain red-top serum; preferred 2 mL serum, minimum 0.25 mL. Separate promptly, freeze and ship on dry ice according to current instructions. Listed analytical turnaround 2-3 days excludes transit. University of Florida, Infectious Disease Pharmacokinetics Laboratory (IDPL) Linezolid: LNZL. Current catalog and requisition ; telephone 352-273-6710. Confirm assay-specific volume and current collection/shipping requirements . The catalog includes other antimycobacterial drug assays. Specify whether the question is a trough or postdose exposure profile. Include exact dose, dosing interval, last administration time, infusion times if applicable, sample time, renal function and relevant MIC. Avoid gel-separator tubes unless explicitly accepted by the performing laboratory. Do not send an untimed “random” linezolid level and interpret it as a trough. Send-out turnaround does not replace prompt action for suspected serious toxicity. Sources [24] [20] [21] [22]

slides.section: Salvage treatment requires evidence and realistic goals
rows: In CONVERT, culture conversion by month six occurred in 29.0% with ALIS plus background therapy versus 8.9% with background therapy alone.
The study enrolled refractory MAC, not all new NTM disease. Respiratory adverse effects are frequent. The 2026 FDA label retains the refractory-MAC indication; use in M. abscessus is off-label.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Salvage treatment requires evidence and realistic goals Evidence for selected treatment options Option What supports it Limit of the evidence ALIS for refractory MAC In CONVERT, culture conversion by month six occurred in 29.0% with ALIS plus background therapy versus 8.9% with background therapy alone. The study enrolled refractory MAC, not all new NTM disease. Respiratory adverse effects are frequent. The 2026 FDA label retains the refractory-MAC indication; use in M. abscessus is off-label. Clofazimine replacing rifampin in MAC A small open-label randomized trial enrolled 40 patients. Six-month conversion was 62% with clofazimine and 58% with rifampin, each combined with ethambutol and a macrolide. Useful support for a selected alternative, not proof of universal interchangeability. Diarrhea, pigmentation, QT effects and access matter. Do not extrapolate pulmonary MAC findings to HIV-associated disseminated MAC. Omadacycline for M. abscessus A 2026 phase 2 trial randomized 66 adults to 300 mg daily or placebo for 84 days. Symptom-response estimates favored omadacycline; nausea and discontinuation remained relevant. Short-term monotherapy research does not establish durable cure or justify routine clinical monotherapy. Use as a specialist-selected off-label component when appropriate. When to consider pulmonary surgery Refer selected patients with localized destructive disease, persistent culture positivity despite an adequate regimen, resistance, substantial hemoptysis or inability to sustain useful medical treatment. Surgery supplements antimicrobial therapy. Assess predicted postoperative reserve, distribution of disease, nutrition, comorbidities and operative expertise. Balance the potential benefit of resection against operative risk and the distribution of disease. Seek a surgical team experienced in NTM disease. When cure is not a realistic near-term endpoint The multisociety guideline recommends discussing treatment goals, potential benefits, adverse effects and the patient's ability and willingness to undertake therapy. Individualize decisions with expert consultation when an effective regimen cannot be tolerated. Associations between culture conversion and survival are subject to confounding. Neither an observational mortality comparison nor a single successful case proves that a particular regimen prolongs survival. Sources [5] [4] [6] [7] [1]

Newer published trial findings are separated from established recommendations. Sources checked October 25, 2026.

Complete source section:
Sources and evidence limits Adult pulmonary treatment recommendations are principally based on the 2020 multisociety guideline. Extrapulmonary recommendations draw on older guidance and species-specific reports and have less certain treatment durations. Monitoring recommendations are drawn from published guidelines and pharmacotherapy literature; many are based on expert consensus rather than comparative trials. Newer published trial findings are separated from established recommendations. Sources checked October 25, 2026. ATS/ERS/ESCMID/IDSA, 2020. Adult pulmonary NTM treatment guideline.
